title: Shape matching drops duplicate shape-name changes

evidence.quote: export interface SlideShape { name: string; text: string; }
The covered fixtures use one shape per name.

reasoning: The public slide model stores shapes as an array and does not state that names are unique, but diffShapes collapses both old and new shapes into Maps keyed by name. With duplicate names, only one old shape is retained and the removal pass treats every old duplicate as present if any new shape with that name exists, so removals or edits can be emitted as the wrong modification or missed entirely.
reproduction: diffModels({kind:'slides', slides:[{id:'1', shapes:[{name:'Body', text:'A'}, {name:'Body', text:'B'}]}]}, {kind:'slides', slides:[{id:'1', shapes:[{name:'Body', text:'A'}]}]}) reports a Body modification from B to A and no removed B shape.
recommendation: Use a stable shape identity from the adapter when available, or preserve multiplicity by grouping duplicate names and pairing within each group by position or text similarity before reporting unmatched additions/removals.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: PowerPoint tests cover edited, added, and removed shapes only with unique shape names.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a slide diff test with two shapes sharing the same name where one duplicate is removed and assert the removed text is reported without inventing a modification against the remaining duplicate.
minimumFixScope: Update SlideShape identity semantics or diffShapes pairing, plus the PowerPoint adapter/tests if a stable shape id is added to the model.
